headline: High: Devin’s broad workspace/OAuth access plus Haystack’s MCP/network surfaces create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading action errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, Slack, GitHub, Jira, Notion, and MCP content in a cloud workspace, while haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs. That creates a plausible bridge for attacker-controlled content to reach Devin’s instruction-following context. The pairwise interaction is documented only by profiles, so uncertainty remains, but the pathway exists in default integrations.
conditions: IF haystack forwards untrusted MCP or REST content into Devin-visible channels, injection is possible.
IF Devin parses repo, ticket, or chat content as instructions without provenance checks, attacker text can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion from MCP/REST outputs into Devin prompts.
Add provenance labels to all external content before Devin reads it.
Restrict Devin to allowlisted MCP servers only.
Require human review for any instruction-like text from haystack.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets such as deploy keys and integration tokens; haystack has broad network egress and MCP access. Even though haystack’s profile only lists anonymous usage statistics, the pair can still leak Devin-held sensitive workspace data if Devin sends context to haystack-backed services or MCP endpoints. The shared integration surface makes this a default-config risk.
conditions: IF Devin passes repo, chat, or secret-bearing context to haystack-connected APIs, leakage occurs.
IF haystack logs or relays retrieved content outside the workspace, sensitive Devin data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Remove secrets from any Devin-to-haystack payloads.
Use a redaction proxy for code, chat, and ticket text.
Limit haystack to non-sensitive corpora only.
Rotate any exposed integration tokens immediately after testing.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP and egress allowlists on both sides.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use broad network egress; haystack can use MCP and network egress. If both operate on the same repo or shared integration target, they can race on mutable resources or overwrite each other’s outputs. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, so the conflict pathway is plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace path, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF haystack and Devin target the same mutable API or MCP resource without locks, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Serialize git writes through one coordinator.
Use branch-per-agent and merge only after review.
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared resources.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared mutable targets.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that acts inside its workspace, and haystack is a search/RAG agent that can surface retrieved content through MCP or APIs. If Devin treats haystack output as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or other actions with real downstream impact. Because Devin has write and integration privileges, the blast radius is larger than a simple bad answer.
conditions: IF Devin consumes haystack output without verification, incorrect retrievals can become actions.
IF haystack returns stale or hallucinated facts into Devin’s workflow, Devin may commit or message based on them.
mitigations: Require a verification step before Devin acts on haystack output.
Constrain haystack to cite sources for every retrieved claim.
Block autonomous commits from unreviewed retrieval results.
Use a second-pass checker on any action-triggering output.
requires-engineering: add policy gates before write or send actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is a closed-source cloud workspace agent that handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, while haystack is open-source and only lists anonymous usage statistics. The profiles do not document residency or DPA alignment, so compliance risk is mainly from unknown handling of Devin’s sensitive data when routed through haystack-connected services. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Devin data includes regulated content and is routed through haystack-hosted services, residency or retention mismatches may arise.
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or retention controls for shared data, compliance gaps are exposed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of haystack-connected flows.
Confirm residency and retention settings for every integration.
Document a DPA before processing customer data.
Minimize logs for any shared workflow.
requires-engineering: implement compliance controls and audit trails for cross-agent data flows.
